replogle_timing_quality.definition: Each whole command starts after the host/core quiet predicate. End load can increase during a run. Per-core other-work fractions were not collected for the pilot; CPU, wall time and start/end load are retained.

qtl_timing_quality.quiet_start: guarded() enforces scripts/quiet_run.py --wait-only with the selected CPUs after cpu_guard.py wait; individual successful quiet samples are not persisted.
qtl_timing_quality.waiting: host.json waited_for_idle_seconds covers only cpu_guard.py wait, not the additional global/core quiet wait. All waits are excluded from command wall seconds.
qtl_timing_quality.cpu_accounting: cpus_busy_seconds includes the measured command; it is not other-work CPU time.
qtl_timing_quality.peak_rss: GNU time maximum RSS is a per-process maximum, not aggregate process-tree memory for multi-process commands.
qtl_timing_quality.readiness_scope: Final readiness time, load averages, selected CPUs and quiet-wait duration are retained; individual ten-second core/load samples are not.
